title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: archive files classified as one object on Windows
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's archive-classification notice and distinguishes its rollout schedule from the roadmap targets. The audit controls, licensing and automatic default are supported; no corrections are needed.

claims.claim: This change belongs to Microsoft Purview Endpoint Data Loss Prevention.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention-Archive File Classification Behavior Change for Windows Endpoints

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The affected organisations use Endpoint DLP on Windows endpoints with archive file classification enabled.
claims.quote: Organizations using Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP on Windows endpoints with archive file classification enabled

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft names .zip and .rar as examples of affected archives.
claims.quote: Archive files such as .zip and .rar files will be classified directly.

claims.claim: Archive files will be classified directly.
claims.quote: Archive files such as .zip and .rar files will be classified directly.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Archive classification will be a single atomic operation on the archive object.
claims.quote: Classification of archive files will occur as a single, atomic operation.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Files inside archives will no longer generate separate classification events.
claims.quote: Individual files contained within an archive will no longer generate separate classification events.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale
claims.claim: Only the outer archive file will be reported in Endpoint DLP events.
claims.quote: Only the outer archive file will be reported in Endpoint DLP events.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the change aligns Windows archive classification with its cloud workloads.
claims.quote: We are updating archive file classification behavior for Microsoft Purview Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) on Windows endpoints to align with classification behavior across Microsoft cloud workloads.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the change improves classification consistency.
claims.quote: This change improves consistency in classification results

claims.claim: Microsoft says the change reduces event-reporting noise.
claims.quote: reduces event-reporting noise

claims.claim: Microsoft says the change improves performance when processing archives.
claims.quote: enhances performance when processing archive files.

claims.claim: Context-based policy evaluation continues to apply to content within archives.
claims.quote: Context-based and sensitivity label-based policy evaluation will continue to apply to content within archive files.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Sensitivity label-based policy evaluation continues to apply to content within archives.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing DLP policy behaviour for evaluating content within archives is unchanged.
claims.quote: Existing DLP policy behavior for evaluating content within archive files is unchanged.

claims.claim: A licence or charge specific to this archive-classification behaviour change is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP archive file classification single atomic outer archive 570965 pricing license charge. Read Purview service description Endpoint DLP entitlement, Endpoint DLP Learn page, roadmap and MC1474107; results on on-demand scan billing concern a different capability.

claims.claim: The roadmap record and Message Center notice describe no meter or consumption charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP archive file classification single atomic outer archive 570965 pricing license charge; read the supplied roadmap description and all of MC1474107 for pricing, meters and consumption charges. Neither record describes one.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing internal documentation describing archive classification.
claims.quote: Review internal documentation that describes archive file classification behavior.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating procedures that reference separate events for files within archives.
claims.quote: Update operational and monitoring procedures if they reference individual event generation for files contained within archives.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends informing compliance and security teams about outer-archive reporting.
claims.quote: Inform compliance and security teams that Endpoint DLP reporting will show events for the outer archive file instead of individual files within the archive.

claims.claim: The notice does not say that the change reads new data.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1474107 What will happen and Compliance considerations for new data access; the notice describes atomic classification and outer-file reporting and says existing content evaluation is unchanged, without asserting new data is read.

claims.claim: The change notice describes no identity or role changes.
claims.quote: Searched: read all of MC1474107 and the roadmap description for identity, roles and permissions changes; neither describes a change to identity or roles.

claims.claim: No new automated action is described beyond the stated classification and reporting change.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1474107 What will happen and Compliance considerations, and roadmap description for new automated actions; they describe archive classification/reporting and unchanged policy evaluation, not a new autonomous action.
